name: the buried branch with no shared words
readme: Same shape as F-00, but the buried branch (turns 17-23) and the back-reference (U-35) never use the seed query's terms. The user talks about how the work finds its own way through the team and names the idea with an invented word.

Lexical-only anchor discovery is expected to FAIL this fixture: the only units sharing the query's surface terms are the plumbing distractors U-5 and A-28. The failure is recorded in gold.json under expected_failures, so it marks where a semantic or term-expansion anchor source has to earn its place.
The test suite checks the no-shared-terms property mechanically, so an edit to the outline cannot quietly make the fixture easy.

replace_turns.U-19: That's how the work finds its own way through the team too. Jobs drift to whoever is least stuck right now, not to whoever the plan named.
replace_turns.A-20: You could take that further in two ways: let the system hand jobs over automatically by measured load, and publish a daily map of where the jobs actually drifted.
replace_turns.U-21: Keep the daily drift map, that is useful. No automatic hand-over: people should still choose, or the drift stops being natural.
replace_turns.A-22: So the map shows the paths and people keep the choice. The drift is observed, not imposed.
replace_turns.U-23: Yes. I'll call it quellow: the work as water, the team as soil.
replace_turns.U-35: No, same principle as quellow: show me where the water went and I decide the changes.
